svg.title: Portable definitions. Target-local data.
svg.desc: All nine Git-owned Fabric items travel together with portable logical IDs. An explicitly attached Bootstrap plan synchronizes the published branch into DEV. Review and commit generated DEV binding changes before freezing the source and promoting reviewed live definitions to initially empty TEST through the native DEV/TEST pipeline. TEST must bind and verify its own data. PROD is separately provisioned and governed by the derived project. Within an attached DEV/TEST Bootstrap plan, eight groups deploy in dependency order: Books, then SeedBooks, which seeds the fictional portfolio; the BookEvents Eventhouse, then its BookSignals KQL database; ComputeBookSignals, after both SeedBooks and BookSignals, which computes the latest week's signals; BooksOntology; then BindBooks, which binds it. PublishBooksKnowledge publishes the approved documents after Books, independently. Git and pipelines copy definitions, not OneLake or KQL data. Production uses a separately reviewed plan with approved ingestion instead of demo seeding. A Git push alone does not run the plan.

g.text: Native Git bootstraps DEV; pipelines promote reviewed business definitions.
Nine Git items. Logical IDs stay portable; physical bindings are resolved in each target.
Inside an attached DEV/TEST Bootstrap plan
Explicit dependencies. Each notebook is deployed before its action runs.
No OneLake or KQL data is copied by Git/pipelines.
Each target owns its data and source bindings.
PROD has a separate release plan.
Omit demo seeding; use approved ingestion.
Do not weaken the DEV/TEST seed guard.
A Git push does not run Bootstrap. Attach the reviewed plan and wait for its actions.
